messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation made no significant difference to Calgary Depression Scale score at 6 months compared with placebo in people with first-episode psychosis.
Sentence: "There also were no significant differences in the Global Assessment of Function symptom score (mean difference, 0.02; 95% CI, -4.60 to 4.94); Global Assessment of Function disability score (mean difference, -0.01; 95% CI, -5.25 to 5.23), or Calgary Depression Scale score (mean difference, -0.39; 95% CI, -2.05 to 1.26) at 6 months."
Measured as: Calgary Depression Scale score
Population: Adults 18 to 65 years within 3 years of first presentation with a functional psychotic disorder
Intervention: Monthly 120 000 IU cholecalciferol for 6 months
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 149
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency was associated with a higher BDI-II depressive symptom score in hemodialysis patients, after adjustment.
Sentence: "Vitamin D deficiency was associated with a 6.00-point higher BDI-II score in the crude model (95% CI 0.07-11.94; p = 0.047) and a 5.05-point higher score after adjustment (95% CI 0.02-10.07; p = 0.049)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (BDI-II score)
Population: Adults undergoing maintenance hemodialysis at a university hospital in southern Brazil (n=91)
Intervention: Vitamin D deficiency (serum 25(OH)D <20 ng/mL), observational exposure
Comparator: Non-deficient participants (25(OH)D >=20 ng/mL)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 91
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed
